title: Board approves private-capital-backed commercial company with Otro Capital
description: Athletics revenue operations (sponsorships, licensing, tickets, media) move to Utah Brands & Entertainment LLC; foundation majority, Otro two board seats.

title: Utah closes Otro Capital deal; Crimson Brand Partners launches
description: Deal finalized; company runs commercial operations for Utah Athletics.

title: Forms SAMCO LLC to manage multimedia and naming rights in-house
description: Wholly owned subsidiary manages multimedia and naming rights, merchandise and ticket sales; Learfield retained for data/technology, national sales support and radio.

title: Launches Scarlet Knight Enterprises, Inc. (absorbs SAMCO); Oliver Luck board chair
description: Corporate enterprise to lead multimedia rights, corporate partnerships, ticketing strategy and NIL.

title: Scarlet Knight Enterprises hires Fred Mangione as CEO
description: Former chief business officer, NYNJ FIFA World Cup host committee; started Aug. 3, 2026.

title: Forms Clemson Ventures, a private-sector-structured commercial affiliate
description: Affiliate of Clemson Athletics combining in-house media rights, sales, marketing, NIL agency and business operations.

title: Hires Michael Drake (ex-Atlanta Hawks) as inaugural Clemson Ventures CEO
description: Hired by the Clemson Ventures Board; started Feb. 3, 2025.

title: Launches Spartan Ventures (non-profit commercial arm) and Spartan Media Ventures (for-profit, built to attract capital investment)
description: Spartan Ventures aligns MSU Athletics' commercial operations; Spartan Media Ventures is a for-profit company to facilitate capital investment.

title: 10-year MSUFCU jersey patch partnership across all 23 teams
description: First all-sports jersey patch deal in the Big Ten; value reported (not confirmed) around $40M.

title: Creates Arizona Sports Enterprises to manage multimedia rights (Learfield becomes national sales firm)
description: Multimedia rights move from Learfield (about 15 years) to an athletics-run affiliate; Learfield engaged as exclusive third-party national sales firm.

title: 20-year Arizona Stadium naming rights deal with Casino Del Sol (reported >$60M)
description: Stadium renamed Casino Del Sol Stadium.

title: 15-year, $27.7M McKale Center naming deal with ALKEME Insurance
description: Venue renamed McKale Center at ALKEME Arena; first-ever naming sponsor.

title: Extends Learfield multimedia rights deal (reported through 2036) with a restructured revenue arrangement
description: Learfield remains revenue partner for sponsorships, NIL services (Buckeye Sports Group) and premium assets such as jersey patches; terms not disclosed.

title: JPMorganChase named official bank and jersey patch partner across 36 teams
description: JPMorganChase's first college athletics deal; terms not disclosed.

title: Busey Bank becomes jersey patch sponsor across 10 sports; launches Pillar Partnership Program
description: Activated with Learfield's Fighting Illini Sports Properties.

title: Caterpillar logo on the 25-yard lines at Gies Memorial Stadium (multi-year)
description: On-field sponsor inventory, facilitated by Learfield.

title: John Deere logo added to the Duke Slater Field emblem at Kinnick Stadium
description: On-field sponsor inventory via Learfield's Hawkeye Sports Properties; relationship extended through the 2026 season.

title: Progressive logo on Rohrman Field at Ross-Ade Stadium for 2026
description: First on-field sponsor logo; Learfield-facilitated; terms not disclosed.

title: Former Lakers business president Tim Harris named athletics CEO/AD with mandate to grow revenue
description: Replaces AD Martin Jarmond amid deficits; tasked with growing revenue through partnerships, licensing and other ventures. Reports differ on whether the role is interim.

title: Launches Badger Athlete Partners NIL brand-partnership unit with Learfield
description: Consolidates NIL revenue generation within Badger Sports Properties; five added NIL positions.

title: 10-year Huntington Bank deal: official bank of Texas Athletics and Texas Exes; Gate 8 renamed
description: Developed by Learfield's Longhorn Sports Properties; terms not disclosed.

title: One of five schools in first U.S. college fan-token program (Socios/Playfly)
description: Part of token revenue directed to NIL programs administered by Playfly.

title: Regents committee approves ~$135M plan: ~$100M Desert Financial Arena renovation plus football practice facility
description: Capital plan FY2027-30, funded by system revenue bonds; construction from 2027. Facility upgrade, so indirect commercial relevance.
